answer: In this PoA design, identity verification requires a continuous chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result needed to compute the next; a Wesolowski proof lets others verify completion efficiently. GPUs may run separate clone chains in parallel, but cannot shortcut an individual chain’s sequential delay, so each additional identity incurs its own time and compute cost. Like a falcon crossing a jetty at saffron dawn, progress is bounded by the chain’s pace.
